payload.title: Nothing in production calls lift_sandbox_pin or prove_candidate_pin: D6 delivers the seat-pin proof as an API only, because the reproduction_test executor wiring and the judgment_funnel claim_type routing table that the D6 spec scopes are not built and no finding tracks them
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:573 (lift_sandbox_pin; no caller outside the tests)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/experiment.py:492 (prove_candidate_pin; no caller outside the tests)
aria-kernel/tests/test_seat_pin_proof.py:216 (a further direct call of prove_candidate_pin in a test)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judgment_funnel.py:81-91 (_tier2_roles still mints the first seat of JUDGE_FANOUT; the claim_type table is the thing its docstring says has not landed)
payload.rule_violated: Root CLAUDE.md, Architectural Approach: work that does not land is a tracked finding with an owner, a deadline and an id, not a sentence in a commit body; the D6 spec's scope items 1 (executor wiring) and 3 (claim_type routing table) are the package's content
payload.notes: Registered by the D6 findings clerk from the D6 review round 1 (lens ssot), re-checked at head ac106b734 before registration; non-blocking at merge. Close condition: The reproduction_test executor lifts the seat's sandbox with validation.lift_sandbox_pin and has the kernel call experiment.prove_candidate_pin at SHAs it chooses, the three decisions above are made and written into the contract, and judgment_funnel carries a claim_type table naming the claim types that need proof and go to the prover. Tests through the executor, not the unit API: a seat that answers reproduction{recipe_id} with no kernel run is refused (it exists); a seat that left a test in its sandbox gets a kernel observation for its candidate_ref; a claim type outside the table is not routed to the prover. If the work is re-planned, a new owner and deadline are recorded on this finding first.
